subject: Transportation Systems
title: 3D-Printed Bridges
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: 3D-Printed Bridges.

hook.text: Amsterdam has a pedestrian bridge printed entirely from stainless steel by a robot welder.

buildup.text: The robot deposited molten metal layer by layer, forming the structure without molds or formwork.

discovery.text: 3D printing reduces waste and allows organic shapes impossible with traditional construction.

twist.text: Printed bridges are small-scale so far. Structural certification for heavy loads hasn't caught up.

climax.text: As printing technology scales and regulations adapt, printed infrastructure could cut costs and build time.

punchline.text: The future bridge might be printed, not poured.
